title: Recognition of symmetric operadic fibrations in the marked model
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent diagrams and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], categorical patterns of [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], and marked simplicial sets of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Write $\langle n\rangle=\{*,1,\ldots,n\}$. A pointed map is inert if each non-basepoint output has exactly one preimage. Let $\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}$ be the pattern on $N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with inert edges marked and, for every $n\geq0$, the cone from $\langle n\rangle$ to its discrete family of $n$ colour projections $\rho_i:\langle n\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$ specified. The family is empty for $n=0$, so its left cone consists of the vertex $\langle0\rangle$. All $2$-simplices of the base are scaled, as in the cited pattern convention. Endow $\mathsf M=\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}}$ with the model structure of [lem-coef-categorical-pattern-model-calculus].

A symmetric infinity operad is an inner fibration $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ with cocartesian lifts of inert pointed maps, equivalences $P_{\langle n\rangle}\simeq P_{\langle1\rangle}^{n}$ induced by colour projections, and mapping-space product equivalences over each pointed map, indexed by its non-basepoint outputs. Mark its inert edges, meaning the $p$-cocartesian edges over inert maps, and call the result $P^{\mathrm{in}}$. Then $P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is fibrant in $\mathsf M$.

Let $r:E\to P$ be a categorical fibration, meaning an inner fibration lifting equivalence edges with prescribed source. Suppose it has $r$-cocartesian lifts of all inert edges of $P$. For $x\in P_{\langle n\rangle}$ and inert projections $x\to x_i$, suppose cocartesian transport induces $E_x\simeq\prod_{i=1}^n E_{x_i}$. For every edge $u:x\to y$ of $P$, $a\in E_x$, $b\in E_y$, and chosen cocartesian projections $b\to b_i$, suppose composition gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}^{u}_E(a,b)\simeq\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{u_i}_E(a,b_i),$$
where $u_i$ is $u$ followed by the corresponding projection of $y$, and the superscript denotes the homotopy fibre of the map on mapping spaces over that edge of $P$. All empty products, both of categories and of spaces, are terminal. Mark exactly the $r$-cocartesian edges over inert edges of $P$, obtaining $E^{\mathrm{in}/P}$. Then the marked map $r:E^{\mathrm{in}/P}\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is a fibration in $\mathsf M$. No cocartesian lifting over active edges and no completeness or presentability of the fibres is required.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Definition 2.1.1.10, Proposition 2.1.4.6 and its categorical-pattern presentation; Definition 2.3.3.28 and Proposition 2.3.3.30, specialized to the identity approximation of P (relative fibre and mapping-product conditions). The colour-projection pattern includes arity zero. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic result.

proof.text: Let $C=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and let $K_n$ be the discrete simplicial set on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Its left cone has just the projection edges from its cone vertex, apart from degeneracies. Each $\rho_i$ is inert, so all edges of the specified cones map into the base marking, including their degenerate edges. There is a small set of cones, one for each natural number, and $K_0=\varnothing$. Thus these data satisfy the categorical-pattern definition. The hypotheses on $p$ give its inner fibration, inert lifts and exactly the prescribed marking. The total space $P$ is a quasicategory: fill an inner horn first in $C$, and then lift that simplex through $p$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10; apply the fully scaled pattern convention of def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy

proof.text: Pull back $p$ along $h:K_n^{\triangleleft}\to C$. Every nondegenerate edge of this cone is an inert color projection; every other edge is degenerate. The assumed inert lifting supplies global $p$-cocartesian lifts of all image edges with every prescribed source. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-base-restriction]: the pullback is a cocartesian fibration and its cocartesian edges are exactly the edges whose images in $P$ are globally $p$-cocartesian. In particular every cocartesian section has inert legs in $P$, as needed in step 3. Straightening identifies the classifying diagram with the fibers $P_{\langle n\rangle}$, $P_{\langle1\rangle}$ and projection transports. Finite products in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ are categorical products. The assumed comparison $P_{\langle n\rangle}\to\prod_iP_{\langle1\rangle}$ is therefore the comparison for this discrete limit. Explicitly, the join-cone mapping formula gives the mapping space from a test cone with vertex $a$ as $H\times^h_V M$, where $H$ is its boundary mapping space, $M=\operatorname{Map}(a,P_{\langle n\rangle})$ and $V=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(a,P_{\langle1\rangle})$. The product property makes $M\to V$ an equivalence; hence restriction to $H$ is an equivalence, the relative-limit square over a point. For $n=0$ this is exactly terminality of $P_{\langle0\rangle}$. This proves condition (iii).

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10 and Remark 2.1.1.14; fully scaled pattern condition (iii)

proof.text:
Take any cocartesian section of that pullback, with inert legs $e_i:y\to y_i$. For any test cone $t=(a\to a_i)$ in $P$, put $M=\operatorname{Map}_P(a,y)$, $V=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_P(a,y_i)$ and $H=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_P(a_i,y_i)$; write $M_C,V_C,H_C$ for their counterparts after applying $p$. The operad mapping axiom identifies the homotopy fiber of $M\to M_C$ over each pointed map $v$ with the fiber of $V\times^h_{V_C}M_C\to M_C$ over $v$. Here the homotopy fiber of $V\times^h_{V_C}M_C\to M_C$ over $v$ is the homotopy fiber of $V\to V_C$ over the image of $v$, by pasting with the homotopy-fiber square of $\{v\}\to M_C$, and the homotopy fiber of a product of maps over a tuple is the product of the homotopy fibers (path spaces and degreewise pullbacks commute with products). The comparison $M\to V\times^h_{V_C}M_C$ lies over the identity of $M_C$ and induces these equivalences on all homotopy fibers over vertices of $M_C$, so the homotopy-fiber detection lemma gives $M\simeq V\times^h_{V_C}M_C$ over $V$ and $M_C$. By the cited join-cone mapping formula, with its naturality for boundary restriction, and the pasting lemma for homotopy pullbacks (used for both displayed reassociations, the square $H\to V\to V_C$ versus $H\to H_C\to V_C$ commuting through $p$), the mapping space from $t$ to this section is
$$H\times^h_V M\simeq H\times^h_{V_C}M_C\simeq H\times^h_{H_C}(H_C\times^h_{V_C}M_C).$$
Here $H\to V$ sends a tuple $h_i:a_i\to y_i$ to its composites with the legs of $t$, and $M\to V$ composes with $e_i$. The last expression is exactly the homotopy pullback of the boundary mapping space and the base cone mapping space in the definition of a $p$-limit diagram. This proves condition (iv) for every section. For $n=0$, $H,V,H_C,V_C$ are points, and the same displayed equation reduces to $M\simeq M_C$, as supplied by the empty-output axiom. All these are spaces retaining the triangle homotopies. No separate relative-product theorem is needed.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10(2); explicit homotopy-pullback calculation from the statements of lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus, lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection and lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting, in the relative-limit convention of def-coef-infinity-relative-cone.

proof.text: Steps 1-3 give conditions (i)-(iv) of pattern-fiberedness for $P^{\mathrm{in}}$. The categorical-pattern model calculus identifies fibered objects with fibrant objects, proving the first assertion for exactly $\mathsf M_{\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}}$, rather than identifying its cone list with a different presentation of preoperads.

source.place: Theorem B.0.20, applied directly to the stated color-projection pattern

proof.text: Form the induced pattern $p^*\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{sym}}$ of [lem-coef-pattern-induced-fibration-test]. Its marked edges are the inert edges of $P$, and its cones are exactly all inert lifts $x\to x_i$ of the color-projection cones. The categorical fibration $r$ is inner, and $E$ is a quasicategory by filling a base inner horn in $P$ and then lifting. Its assumed inert lifts and specified exact marking give conditions (i)-(ii). For each specified cone $h:K_n^{\triangleleft}\to P$, every image edge is inert or degenerate, so the global $r$-cocartesian lifts with prescribed source required by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-base-restriction] exist. That node gives a cocartesian pullback and identifies all its cocartesian edges with globally $r$-cocartesian edges in $E$. Thus every section considered in step 6 satisfies the hypothesis on cocartesian projections, not just sections chosen in advance. Straightening identifies the classifying diagram with $E_x\to E_{x_i}$. The assumed comparison $E_x\simeq\prod_iE_{x_i}$ proves condition (iii): the discrete join-cone formula of step 2 applies verbatim, with $M=\operatorname{Map}(a,E_x)$ and $V=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}(a,E_{x_i})$, so $M\to V$ is an equivalence and $H\times^h_V M\to H$ is an equivalence for every test cone. For $n=0$ this uses the assumed terminal fiber $E_x$.

source.place: Remark B.0.27; Definition 2.3.3.28 relative product conditions, applied to the identity approximation

proof.text:
For any cocartesian section of the last pullback, write its vertex as $b\in E_x$ and its legs as $b\to b_i\in E_{x_i}$. For any test cone $t=(a\to a_i)$ in $E$, put $M=\operatorname{Map}_E(a,b)$, $V=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_E(a,b_i)$, and $H=\prod_i\operatorname{Map}_E(a_i,b_i)$; write $M_P,V_P,H_P$ for their counterparts after applying $r$. The assumed relative output axiom for every edge $u:r(a)\to x$ identifies the fibers over $u$. As in step 3, the homotopy fiber of $V\times^h_{V_P}M_P\to M_P$ over $u$ is, by pasting, the homotopy fiber of $V\to V_P$ over the image of $u$, namely $\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{u_i}_E(a,b_i)$. The comparison $M\to V\times^h_{V_P}M_P$ lies over the identity of $M_P$ and is an equivalence on every such homotopy fiber, so the homotopy-fiber detection lemma gives $M\simeq V\times^h_{V_P}M_P$ over $V$ and $M_P$. The join-cone mapping formula and the pasting lemma for homotopy pullbacks now give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_n^{\triangleleft},E)}(t,s)\simeq H\times^h_V M\simeq H\times^h_{V_P}M_P\simeq H\times^h_{H_P}(H_P\times^h_{V_P}M_P).$$
The maps $H\to V$ and $M\to V$ compose with the legs of $t$ and $s$, respectively. The last expression is exactly the homotopy pullback required in the defining relative-limit square, with boundary mapping space $H$ and base cone mapping space $H_P\times^h_{V_P}M_P$. Thus $s$ is an $r$-limit diagram, proving condition (iv). For $n=0$ the four product spaces are points and the calculation reduces to $M\simeq M_P$, which is the empty-product mapping hypothesis. The mapping fibers here are over edges of $P$; no identification with fibers over $C$ is made.

source.place: Definition 2.3.3.28(3); explicit homotopy-pullback calculation from the statements of lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus, lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection and lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting, in the relative-limit convention of def-coef-infinity-relative-cone.

proof.text: Thus $r:E^{\mathrm{in}/P}\to P^{\mathrm{in}}$ is fibered for the induced pattern. Every equivalence in $C=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ comes from a pointed bijection, and each such bijection is inert; all triangles are scaled. The target is pattern-fibered by step 4, so all hypotheses of the induced-pattern fibration test hold. It follows that $r$ is a fibration in $\mathsf M$. Only the displayed inert lifts, fiber products and relative mapping products entered the argument; it requires neither active cocartesian lifts nor any completeness or presentability of the fibers.

source.place: Proposition B.2.7, (c) implies (a), for the specified symmetric pattern

proof_origin.place: Direct verification of fully scaled color-projection pattern conditions; Remark B.0.27 and Proposition B.2.7. Relative mapping-space bridge is calculated in steps 3 and 6 from the existing join-cone formula; see second-reading report.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q129-066c07264 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 12 cited node statements and Lurie's Higher Algebra (HA) at the cited places in full. HA is not archived in literature/, so I read a local /tmp copy: Def 2.1.1.10, Rem 2.1.1.14 (3'), Prop 2.1.4.6 and its proof (HA uses the binary pattern), Rem B.0.27 and Prop B.2.7. The statement is true and unchanged. It is stated for the DAG's own all-colour discrete-cone pattern, including n=0, and is not identified with HA's binary presentation. It touches no coefficient category or base-change morphism and uses no SGA source. The repaired steps 2 and 5 now cite lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-base-restriction, and its hypotheses hold. For p and for r the total spaces are quasicategories and T=K_n^cone is a poset nerve. Every image edge is a colour projection or an identity, and identities are inert, so the inert-lift hypotheses cover both. The lemma's characterisation of cocartesian edges shows that every cocartesian section has inert legs. Condition (iii) follows from straightening, categorical products in Cat_infinity and the join-cone formula. Steps 3 and 6 are correct: fibre detection over the identity base map, the HA 2.1.1.10(2) and relative mapping products, and pasting twice give exactly the relative-limit square; the step-6 fibres are over edges of P. Step 4 identifies fibered with fibrant objects. Step 7 applies the induced-pattern test (c)=>(a): equivalences in Fin_* are bijections, hence inert, and all triangles are scaled. Small cases: for n=0 the empty products are terminal or contractible and are kept; n=1 gives the unary comparison; empty fibres are allowed. All proof deps are in the item's unit, none is merged, so no tool_uses are needed. The base-restriction node is unsplit, so there is no cycle. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, there are no TeX escape faults and no new nodes.
